Packaging claim: Standing Toilet Water Is the Sewer-Gas Seal
Core fact: A toilet retains water in its curved trapway; this water forms a barrier to sewer gas.
Second reveal: When a trap dries out, that water barrier disappears and sewer gas can pass through the drain path.
First-frame and mechanism proof: A clearly labelled licensed or owned local cutaway video showing standing water retained in the toilet trap. Show the wet versus dry path; do not pass an illustration off as camera footage.
Search queries: toilet trap cutaway; toilet p trap water seal; toilet plumbing diagram
Fact boundaries: Avoid diagnosing plumbing problems or claiming all odors come from a dry trap. Focus on the trap-seal principle.
